classification.difficultyReason: Combines equal angles in isosceles and equilateral triangles with straight-line, vertically opposite and reflex-angle relationships.

children.label: m
children.prompt: Find the size of the shaded angle.

spec.description: Two isosceles triangles share a vertical side. A shaded sector spans both lower angles.
spec.mathematics: The left triangle has equal outer sides and a 40° upper base angle. The right triangle has equal outer sides and a 40° apex angle. The requested combined lower angle is 40° + 70°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the two 40° givens are visible; the shaded target has no supplied answer.

answer.worked:
The lower angle in the left triangle is $40^\circ$ because base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.

Let $b$ be the lower angle in the right triangle.
$$\begin{align*}b+b+40&=180\\2b+40&=180\\2b&=140\\b&=70^\circ\end{align*}$$
The shaded angle is $40^\circ+70^\circ=110^\circ$.

spec.description: A triangle lies below a sloping line extended past both upper vertices.
spec.mathematics: The exterior angles at the upper vertices are 126° and 115°. Their adjacent interior angles are 54° and 65°; p is the third interior angle.
spec.answerVisibility: 126°, 115° and p are visible. The answer 61° is excluded.

answer.worked:
The two upper interior angles are $180^\circ-126^\circ=54^\circ$ and $180^\circ-115^\circ=65^\circ$ because angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.

Using the angle sum of a triangle:
$$\begin{align*}p+54+65&=180\\p+119&=180\\p&=61^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: A triangle stands above a slightly sloping baseline extended at both ends.
spec.mathematics: The left interior angle is 80°, the right exterior angle is 135°, and p is the apex angle.
spec.answerVisibility: 80°, 135° and p are visible. The supplied 55° answer is excluded.

answer.worked:
The right interior angle is $180^\circ-135^\circ=45^\circ$ because angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.

Using the angle sum of a triangle:
$$\begin{align*}p+80+45&=180\\p+125&=180\\p&=55^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: An isosceles triangle has equal base and right side, an apex angle of 74°, and a reflex angle y outside its left base vertex.
spec.mathematics: The interior angle opposite the right side equals the 74° apex angle opposite the base. The requested reflex angle is 360° − 74°.
spec.answerVisibility: 74° and the reflex-angle label y° are visible; 286° is excluded.

answer.worked:
The left interior angle is $74^\circ$ because angles opposite equal sides are equal.

Angles at a point sum to $360^\circ$:
$$\begin{align*}y+74&=360\\y&=286^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.label: q
children.prompt: This is a pair of overlapping equilateral triangles. Find every angle.

spec.description: Two equilateral triangles overlap. One points upward with a horizontal base; the other points downward with a sloping upper side. A 45° given lies above the horizontal base and to the left of the descending side at their crossing.
spec.mathematics: The six triangle vertices are 60°. The confirmed 45° crossing determines the relative orientation and all remaining angles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the 45° given confirmed in the original unsolved Word image is visible. Completed answer annotations are separated into the solution diagram.

answer.short: Every triangle vertex is $60^\circ$. At the base crossing, the angles alternate $45^\circ,135^\circ$. At the upper crossing, they alternate $75^\circ,105^\circ$. Each junction on a triangle side has $45^\circ,60^\circ,75^\circ$; see the labelled figure.
answer.worked:
Each vertex angle of an equilateral triangle is $60^\circ$.

At the crossing on the horizontal base, the opposite angle is $45^\circ$ because vertically opposite angles are equal. Each adjacent angle is $180^\circ-45^\circ=135^\circ$.

The lower-left small triangle has angles $60^\circ$, $45^\circ$ and $a$:
$$\begin{align*}a+60+45&=180\\a+105&=180\\a&=75^\circ\end{align*}$$
At that junction, the remaining angle on the straight side is $180^\circ-75^\circ-60^\circ=45^\circ$.

The upper small triangle has angles $60^\circ$, $45^\circ$ and $b$:
$$\begin{align*}b+60+45&=180\\b+105&=180\\b&=75^\circ\end{align*}$$
At the upper crossing, its opposite angle is $75^\circ$ and each adjacent angle is $180^\circ-75^\circ=105^\circ$.

The upper-right small triangle has angles $60^\circ$, $75^\circ$ and $c$:
$$\begin{align*}c+60+75&=180\\c+135&=180\\c&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$
At the right-hand junction on the horizontal base, the remaining angle is $180^\circ-45^\circ-60^\circ=75^\circ$. All angles are labelled in the solution figure.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 14, part q, completed answer figure
spec.description: The overlapping equilateral triangles have every angular region labelled, including the two vertically opposite regions left unlabelled in the supplied answer figure.
spec.mathematics: Six 60° vertex sectors; four 45° sectors; four 75° sectors; two 105° crossing sectors; two 135° crossing sectors. The original answer figure labels only one of each 105° and 135° pair.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only. Retains all supplied answer positions and completes the two unlabelled vertically opposite sectors.

children.label: r
children.prompt: This is a pair of isosceles triangles. Work out the size of angle $y$.

spec.description: Two isosceles triangles share their lower-left vertex. The narrow upright triangle has double side ticks and a 40° apex. The broader triangle has single ticks, a 30° lower-left angle and a lower diagonal meeting the upright triangle's right side at 90°. The angle y lies between that diagonal and the horizontal base.
spec.mathematics: The upright triangle's base angles are 70°. The right-angled triangle formed by its right side, base and the diagonal has angles 70°, 90° and y. The broader triangle's 30° angle and equal-side marks are retained as redundant givens.
spec.answerVisibility: 40°, 30°, 90° and y are visible. The supplied 20° answer is excluded.

answer.worked:
Let $b$ be a base angle of the upright isosceles triangle. Its base angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}b+b+40&=180\\2b+40&=180\\2b&=140\\b&=70^\circ\end{align*}$$
The small triangle below the marked intersection has angles $70^\circ$, $90^\circ$ and $y$. The angle at the intersection is $90^\circ$ because vertically opposite angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}y+70+90&=180\\y+160&=180\\y&=20^\circ\end{align*}$$
